In each cell, the upper line is generation time; the lower line is wall runtime per phase-space point.  The left slot is the generated-library \AC\ reference value, the middle slot is \PAC\ JIT, and the right slot is \PAC\ C++ O3. Runtime multipliers are shown as \texttt{(wall|core)}. When no \AC\ reference exists but \PAC\ ran, the \PAC\ slots show absolute generation time and parenthesized \texttt{wall|core} runtime in microseconds. For NLC/full-colour tables, \AC\ reference values come from the dedicated \texttt{amplicol\_color\_probe} imode-2 colour-matrix driver rather than the LC generated-library timing driver. Colored ratios are \PAC/\AC: green below one, orange below two, red otherwise.  When rows are generated with \texttt{--validate}, \PAC\ JIT and C++ O3 values are compared to the same-point \AC\ value with a relative tolerance of \(10^{-8}\).

\paragraph{Matrix run settings.}
The matrix table is generated with one uniform benchmark setup. The full refresh command is:
\begin{lstlisting}[language=bash,breaklines=true,breakatwhitespace=true]
pyAmpliCol/dependencies/.venv/bin/python pyAmpliCol/docs/result_matrix.py --color-accuracy nlc --data /Users/vjhirsch/HEP_programs/AmpliCol/pyAmpliCol/docs/result_matrix_nlc_data.json --table /Users/vjhirsch/HEP_programs/AmpliCol/pyAmpliCol/docs/result_matrix_nlc_table.tex --generate-data 1-9 --show-data 1-9 --time-limit 900 --target-runtime 1 --amplicol-points 10000 --jobs 4 --n-cores 4 --process-workers 1 --columns-per-table 3
\end{lstlisting}
\noindent\footnotesize Partial refreshes use the same settings with \texttt{--base-process}, \texttt{--skip-jit}, \texttt{--skip-cpp-o3}, \texttt{--process-ids}, or \texttt{--skip-amplicol} added only to restrict which cells are updated.  PyAmpliCol-only refreshes may additionally use \texttt{--process-workers 5}; this is intentionally disabled when the \AC\ reference is refreshed because that path uses shared top-level generated-library files.  \AC\ reference timings for this colour table currently use the dedicated \texttt{amplicol\_color\_probe} imode-2 colour-matrix driver, not integration-driver timings.  The driver exposes the same absolute \AC\ NLC/full-colour matrix element and splits amplitude-evaluation from colour-contraction time, but it is not yet a generated-library driver.  \PAC\ rows use the generic staged-DAG artifact, Rusticol double precision, JIT or C++ O3 Symbolica evaluators as labelled, and \texttt{time-process} with a one-second target runtime.  The \texttt{--time-limit} setting applies only to C++ O3 generation; \AC\ and JIT rows are left uncapped.
\par\smallskip
\paragraph{C++ O3 compile-budget gaps.}
The following cells have validated \AC\ and \PAC\ JIT rows but no completed C++ O3 row; their C++ slot is a localized performance-generation compile-budget gap, not a physics-validation failure: $gg\to t\bar t+(n-2)g$, \(n=4\): timed out; $gg\to gg+(n-2)g$, \(n=4\): timed out.
\par\smallskip
